<!-- 01 ABOUT -->
<section class="numbered" id="about">
  <div class="num-head"><div class="num">01</div><h2>About</h2></div>
  <div class="num-body">
    <p class="lead-p">I work at the intersection of rigorous statistical methodology and applied biomedical research — designing analyses that hold up to scrutiny and translate into evidence that clinicians, investigators, and communities can use.</p>
    <p>Before beginning my PhD in Biostatistics at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, I worked at the University of Texas at El Paso's Border Biomedical Research Center, supporting studies in cardiometabolic disease, inflammatory aging, cancer, and health disparities. I have contributed to federally funded projects, including the <em>All of Us</em> Research Program.</p>
    <p>I'm both a research statistician and a data analytics professional. I use R and Python for statistical modeling — survival analysis, causal inference, general and generalized linear models, and linear mixed models — and SQL, Tableau and CRM data for descriptive and predictive analytics with higher-education and research data.</p>
